sentences.en: In 1928, a strange phenomenon was sweeping the state of Idaho.
sentences.zh: 1928年，一种奇怪的现象席卷了爱达荷州。

sentences.en: A vanishing act of sorts.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，这是一种“消失术”。

sentences.en: A Boise resident would wake up on a typical Monday morning,
sentences.zh: 博伊西的居民在某个平常的周一早晨醒来，

sentences.en: drag themselves out of bed, get dressed for the day,
sentences.zh: 从床上爬起来，穿好衣服准备开始新的一天，

sentences.en: and they would hop in their car to drive to work,
sentences.zh: 然后跳上车开车去上班，

sentences.en: not noticing that something was missing.
sentences.zh: 却没注意到少了点什么。

sentences.en: And suddenly, cops in the rear view.
sentences.zh: 突然，后视镜里出现了警察。

sentences.en: The next thing that the driver of the car knew,
sentences.zh: 司机还没反应过来是怎么回事，

sentences.en: they were getting picked up because they weren't displaying a license plate.
sentences.zh: 就被拦下了，因为他们的车上没挂牌照。

sentences.en: Idaho historian Rick Just says license plates?
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州历史学家里克·贾斯特说，牌照？

sentences.en: Well, they were disappearing.
sentences.zh: 它们消失了。

sentences.en: The Secretary of State was fielding complaints about all the lost tags.
sentences.zh: 州务卿一直在处理关于牌照丢失的投诉。

sentences.en: And soon enough, the culprit became clear.
sentences.zh: 很快，罪魁祸首就浮出水面了。

sentences.en: Tourists would come to Idaho and steal the plates.
sentences.zh: 游客来到爱达荷州，顺手偷走了这些牌照。

sentences.en: Idaho's license plates were being snatched up like plush hotel bathrobes.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州的牌照就像酒店里的毛绒浴袍一样被抢购一空。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: People would come up, but they would pull up to either a tourist park or a motel or something,
sentences.zh: 人们开车过来，停在旅游公园、汽车旅馆之类的地方，

sentences.en: and they would spot those plates and think,
sentences.zh: 看到那些牌照就会想，

sentences.en: you know, I'd like to have a souvenir.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想要个纪念品。

sentences.en: And so they would just take it off of the car and take it home.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就直接把牌照从车上拆下来带回家了。

sentences.en: And there was a reason why people couldn't resist swiping Idaho plates in particular.
sentences.zh: 人们之所以对爱达荷州的牌照情有独钟，是有原因的。

sentences.en: That year, the state had revolutionized license plate design.
sentences.zh: 那一年，该州彻底革新了牌照设计。

sentences.en: That's reporter Daniel Ackerman.
sentences.zh: 这是记者丹尼尔·阿克曼。

sentences.en: Before this, plates were basic,
sentences.zh: 在此之前，牌照都很基础，

sentences.en: with info like the state name and the registration numbers.
sentences.zh: 上面只有州名和注册号码等信息。

sentences.en: All of this on a pretty simple, solid-colored background.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都印在简单、纯色的背景上。

sentences.en: But in 1928, the Secretary of State in Idaho had an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 但在1928年，爱达荷州州务卿灵光一现。

sentences.en: He was like, we have this half-square foot of open real estate
sentences.zh: 他想，我们有这半平方英尺的空地，

sentences.en: just rolling around on everyone's cars.
sentences.zh: 在每个人的车上晃来晃去。

sentences.en: Let's do something with it.
sentences.zh: 我们得利用起来。

sentences.en: The 1928 plate is often said to be the very first advertising license plate in the country.
sentences.zh: 1928年的那块牌照通常被认为是全国第一块广告牌照。

sentences.en: The very first one that tried to advertise a product.
sentences.zh: 第一块试图推销产品的牌照。

sentences.en: And the product that Idaho chose will surprise absolutely no one.
sentences.zh: 而爱达荷州选择的产品绝对不会让任何人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The state's 1928 license plates all featured a single, giant potato.
sentences.zh: 该州1928年的所有牌照上都印着一颗巨大的土豆。

sentences.en: A big, kind of elongated, goofy-looking potato, but big.
sentences.zh: 一颗又大、形状有点长、看起来傻乎乎的土豆，但确实很大。

sentences.en: It was almost as big as the plate.
sentences.zh: 它几乎和牌照一样大。

sentences.en: The registration numbers were stamped in green lettering,
sentences.zh: 注册号码用绿色字体印着，

sentences.en: right on top of this lumpy, brown spud.
sentences.zh: 就印在这块凹凸不平的棕色土豆上。

sentences.en: I would say it looks almost fecal in nature.
sentences.zh: 我会说它看起来甚至有点像粪便。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: The shape, particularly.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那个形状。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The execution wasn't perfect, but it was innovative.
sentences.zh: 虽然设计并不完美，但很有创意。

sentences.en: Below the tremendous tater, there was even a modest, pragmatic slogan.
sentences.zh: 在这颗巨大的土豆下方，甚至还有一句朴实、务实的口号。

sentences.en: Idaho potatoes.
sentences.zh: “爱达荷土豆”。

sentences.en: Today, every state's got a marketing slogan.
sentences.zh: 如今，每个州都有自己的营销口号。

sentences.en: Hawaii is the Aloha state.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷是“阿罗哈之州”。

sentences.en: Missouri is the Show Me state.
sentences.zh: 密苏里是“向我展示之州”。

sentences.en: But Idaho was the first to put theirs on a license plate.
sentences.zh: 但爱达荷州是第一个把口号印在牌照上的。

sentences.en: They wanted to make sure that when people thought about Idaho,
sentences.zh: 他们想确保当人们想到爱达荷州时，

sentences.en: they thought potatoes.
sentences.zh: 就能想到土豆。

sentences.en: And for better or worse, the association stuck.
sentences.zh: 不管好坏，这个联想算是扎根了。

sentences.en: And now it's gotten to be such a thing.
sentences.zh: 现在这已经成了一种传统。

sentences.en: I mean, coming up here in a few days at New Year's Eve, we drop a potato.
sentences.zh: 我是说，再过几天就是除夕了，我们要举行“降土豆”仪式。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, you know how the Times Square ball comes floating down like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道时代广场的水晶球是怎么缓缓降下的吧。

sentences.en: Well, we have a big potato that comes floating down.
sentences.zh: 我们也有一个大土豆缓缓降下。

sentences.en: They've been doing it about 10 years now.
sentences.zh: 他们已经这么做了大约10年了。

sentences.en: The concept of slapping a tagline onto a license plate might not seem like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 在牌照上贴标语的概念看起来可能没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: But it turns out this idea would end up having outsized consequences.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这个想法最终产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And not just for Idaho.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是对爱达荷州而言。

sentences.en: We're talking legislative clashes, multiple Supreme Court cases, and even jail time.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是立法冲突、多起最高法院案件，甚至还有牢狱之灾。

sentences.en: Because what started in one state would soon spread.
sentences.zh: 因为始于一个州的想法很快就会蔓延开来。

sentences.en: And when it did, the question of what should go on a license plate and what shouldn't
sentences.zh: 当它蔓延时，关于牌照上该印什么、不该印什么的问题，

sentences.en: would prove surprisingly contentious.
sentences.zh: 事实证明争议出奇地大。

sentences.en: The first state-issued license plates appeared at the very beginning of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 州政府发放的第一批牌照出现在20世纪初。

sentences.en: And they served a mostly bureaucratic function.
sentences.zh: 它们主要起着官僚管理的作用。

sentences.en: More people were buying and crashing cars every year.
sentences.zh: 每年买车和撞车的人越来越多。

sentences.en: So state governments originally mandated plates as a way to keep track of all the nuts behind
sentences.zh: 所以州政府最初强制要求挂牌照，是为了追踪所有在方向盘后的疯子。

sentences.en: the wheel.
sentences.zh: 当时没人对打广告感兴趣。

sentences.en: No one was interested in sloganeering.
sentences.zh: 但后来美国人发现了公路旅行的乐趣。

sentences.en: But then Americans discovered the road trip.
sentences.zh: “开着你的雪佛兰看美国”。

sentences.en: See the USA in your Chevrolet.
sentences.zh: 汽车普及带来的一个重要因素是，它让人们获得了漫游的自由。

sentences.en: Well, the big factor with increase in automobiles was that it allowed people freedom to roam.
sentences.zh: 你可以去任何你想去的地方。

sentences.en: You could go wherever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀·拜伦是大急流城公共图书馆的前历史馆员。

sentences.en: Christine Byron is a former history librarian at the Grand Rapids Public Library.
sentences.zh: 她专注于旅游史。

sentences.en: She focuses on the history of tourism.
sentences.zh: 她说，20世纪20年代公路旅行的兴起创造了一个巨大的新旅游市场。

sentences.en: And she says that the rise of the road trip in the 1920s created this huge new tourist market.
sentences.zh: 司机们需要加油站和路边汽车旅馆等服务，这些在蒸汽动力旅行时代是不存在的。

sentences.en: Drivers needed services like gas stations and roadside motels that hadn't existed in the
sentences.zh: 当你乘坐汽船或火车旅行时，你基本上带上了你需要的一切。

sentences.en: age of steam-powered travel.
sentences.zh: 而且你的餐点是在度假村供应的。

sentences.en: When you traveled by steamship or railroad, you pretty much brought what you needed with you.
sentences.zh: 但一旦汽车出现，就需要花更多的钱。

sentences.en: And your meals were served at a resort.
sentences.zh: 从州政府的角度来看，所有这些新的旅游资金都唾手可得。

sentences.en: But once the automobile came along, there was a lot more money that needed to be spent.
sentences.zh: 于是各州开始向世界宣传他们能提供什么。

sentences.en: From the state's perspective, all those new tourist dollars were up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州有大峡谷。

sentences.en: So states started letting the world know what they had to offer.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州有湖泊。

sentences.en: Arizona had the Grand Canyon.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州有平均每年310天的阳光。

sentences.en: Minnesota, its lakes.
sentences.zh: 在这场争夺游客的战争中，各州尽可能地推销自己。

sentences.en: New Mexico, its average 310 days of sunshine per year.
sentences.zh: 全国性杂志、各种汽车指南、《蓝色指南》、《绿皮书》，

sentences.en: And in this war for tourists, states promoted themselves anywhere they could.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有海量的宣传册。

sentences.en: National magazines, various automobile guides, the Blue Guide, the Green Book,
sentences.zh: 但没人想到在牌照上做广告。

sentences.en: and of course, tons and tons of promotional brochures.
sentences.zh: 直到1928年，爱达荷人意识到他们的牌照太有价值了，不能只印个注册号码。

sentences.en: But no one thought to advertise on a license plate.
sentences.zh: 里克·贾斯特说，一旦爱达荷州在牌照上插上了他们的淀粉旗帜，

sentences.en: Until 1928, when Idahoans realized that their plates were too valuable to waste
sentences.zh: 热潮就开始了。

sentences.en: on just a registration number.
sentences.zh: 因为那个土豆，牌照变成了另一种东西。

sentences.en: And Rick Just says once Idaho staked its starchy flag on the license plate,
sentences.zh: 各州在世纪中叶花费时间将他们的牌照，

sentences.en: the rush was on.
sentences.zh: 从严肃的政府文件变成了旅游和工业的彩色助推器。

sentences.en: License plates became a different thing because of that potato.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以把它们看作是，你知道，在全州乃至全国行驶的微型小广告。

sentences.en: States spent the middle of the century transforming their plates
sentences.zh: 1940年，亚利桑那州在牌照上印上了“大峡谷之州”，从此一发不可收拾。

sentences.en: from austere government documents into colorful boosters of tourism and industry.
sentences.zh: 1950年，明尼苏达州选择了“万湖之国”。

sentences.en: You could even think of them as, you know, miniature little ads that are driving,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，新墨西哥州实际上在1932年就把“阳光之州”印在了牌照上，

sentences.en: you know, all over the state and all over the country, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 比佛罗里达州在1949年抢走这个口号要早。

sentences.en: In 1940, Arizona stamped Grand Canyon State on its plates and never looked back.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，佛罗里达州平均每年只有237天的阳光。

sentences.en: In 1950, Minnesota went with land of 10,000 lakes.
sentences.zh: 但无所谓了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, New Mexico actually put Sunshine State on its plates in 1932,
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州是“美国的勇敢之地”。

sentences.en: before Florida muscled in on the slogan in 1949.
sentences.zh: 缅因州是“度假胜地”。

sentences.en: Florida, for the record, only has an average of 237 days of sunshine per year.
sentences.zh: 其他州则犹豫不决。

sentences.en: But whatever.
sentences.zh: 例如，密歇根州的牌照最初在1954年印着“水上仙境”。

sentences.en: Wisconsin was America's daring land.
sentences.zh: 后来演变成了“冬季水上仙境”。

sentences.en: Maine was vacation land.
sentences.zh: 随后是“五大湖之州”、“五大湖”和“五大湖之美”。

sentences.en: Other states couldn't make up their minds.
sentences.zh: 1970年，密歇根州旅游委员会实际上采纳了这一口号：

sentences.en: Michigan's plate, for example, initially sported the phrase water wonderland in 1954.
sentences.zh: “密歇根，五大湖的准岛屿”。

sentences.en: Which then evolved into winter water wonderland.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，那块牌照从未问世。

sentences.en: Followed by Great Lakes State, Great Lakes, and Great Lakes Splendor.
sentences.zh: 如今，像这样的牌照已成为一种国家制度。

sentences.en: In 1970, Michigan's State Tourism Council actually adopted the slogan,
sentences.zh: 而且以一种俗气的美国风情来看，这很有趣。

sentences.en: The Michigans, the almost islands of the Great Lakes.
sentences.zh: 每个州都在真诚地展示自己最好的一面。

sentences.en: But sadly, that plate never happened.
sentences.zh: 那么这里会有什么问题呢？

sentences.en: Today, license plates like these are a national institution.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，问题还不少。

sentences.en: And it's fun, in a kitschy Americana kind of way.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管其中一些牌照可能很有趣，

sentences.en: Each state is earnestly trying to put its best foot forward.
sentences.zh: 但半平方英尺的牌照毕竟是一个很小的画布。

sentences.en: So what could possibly be wrong here?
sentences.zh: 当你必须选择一个符号来代表整个州时，

sentences.en: It turns out, quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 你不可能让每个人都满意。

sentences.en: Because as fun as some of these plates might have been,
sentences.zh: 这从一开始就引起了麻烦。

sentences.en: at half a square foot, a license plate is a small canvas.
sentences.zh: 1928年，当爱达荷州推出土豆牌照时，反响并不好。

sentences.en: And when you have to pick one symbol to represent an entire state,
sentences.zh: 人们讨厌那些牌照。

sentences.en: you are not going to please everyone.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，许多爱达荷人反感与该州的经济作物联系在一起。

sentences.en: And this has caused trouble from the get-go.
sentences.zh: 特别是北爱达荷州的人，因为他们那里不种土豆。

sentences.en: In 1928, when Idaho unleashed the potato plates, it didn't go over all that well.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这主要是爱达荷州东南部的事情。

sentences.en: People detested those license plates.
sentences.zh: 报纸社论称其为一种尴尬。

sentences.en: Lots of Idahoans, it turned out, resented being associated with the state's cash crop.
sentences.zh: 一个标题甚至写道：

sentences.en: Particularly people from northern Idaho, because they don't grow potatoes up there.
sentences.zh: “为什么要提那个？”

sentences.en: Really, it's a kind of a southeastern Idaho thing.
sentences.zh: 他们最终在1929年完全放弃了这个想法，回归到纯数字，这大概是件好事。

sentences.en: Newspaper editorials called it an embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 没有座右铭，没有图形。

sentences.en: One headline actually read,
sentences.zh: 当然也没有土豆。

sentences.en: Why bring that up?
sentences.zh: 牌照纠纷并非爱达荷州独有。

sentences.en: And probably it's a good thing that they just dropped the idea entirely and went back to numbers in 1929.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州不得不废弃其中一款牌照设计，因为居民抱怨带梗的葡萄看起来更像炸弹。

sentences.en: No motto, no graphics.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，马萨诸塞州试图在州名旁边放一条鳕鱼，

sentences.en: And certainly no potatoes.
sentences.zh: 结果被渔民指责导致当年捕鱼量不佳，

sentences.en: And license plate quarrels weren't unique to Idaho.
sentences.zh: 因为牌照上的鱼正游离“马萨诸塞”这个词。

sentences.en: Florida had to dump one of its plate designs after residents complained that the grapefruit with a stem attached looked more like a bomb.
sentences.zh: 这些关于牌照设计的争吵看起来可能只是小事一桩。

sentences.en: Massachusetts, meanwhile, tried to put a codfish right next to its state's name,
sentences.zh: 但关于牌照的斗争即将升级，

sentences.en: only to be blamed by fishermen for a poor catch that year,
sentences.zh: 多亏了一位名叫梅尔德拉姆·汤普森的政客。

sentences.en: because the fish on the plate was swimming away from the word Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 在这场关乎美国生存的关键战役中，

sentences.en: These dust-ups over license plate design can seem like small potatoes.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不容忍没有赢家的妥协。

sentences.en: But the fight over license plates was about to be taken to the next level,
sentences.zh: 汤普森是20世纪70年代新罕布什尔州政坛的巨人。

sentences.en: thanks to a politician named Meldrum Thompson.
In this critical battle for the survival of America,
we shall not tolerate a no-win settlement.

He served three terms as governor, and he was a conservative firebrand who hated Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他曾三度担任州长，是一位痛恨民主党人的保守派激进分子。

sentences.en: We must drive from the seats of power in the White House, Congress, and the State Department
sentences.zh: 我们必须将那些身居白宫、国会和国务院高位的人赶下台，

sentences.zh: 把所有那些共产主义同情者的余孽统统赶走。

sentences.en: Thompson had a lot of unorthodox ideas,
sentences.zh: 汤普森有很多非传统的想法，

sentences.zh: 包括想给新罕布什尔州国民警卫队配备核武器。

sentences.en: And he was obsessed with freedom.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常痴迷于自由。

sentences.en: Here's Thompson's dorky campaign song.
sentences.zh: 这是汤普森那首傻气的竞选歌曲。

sentences.en: Live free or die, of course, is New Hampshire's fiery state motto.
sentences.zh: “不自由，毋宁死”，这当然是新罕布什尔州那句激昂的州格言。

sentences.en: It was coined by a Revolutionary War vet.
sentences.zh: 它是由一位独立战争的老兵创造的。

sentences.en: And Thompson loved it so much that before he became governor,
sentences.zh: 汤普森非常喜欢这句话，以至于在他担任州长之前，

sentences.en: he worked with allies in the state legislature to get it slapped on every car in the state.
sentences.zh: 他就与州议会的盟友合作，让它出现在该州的每一辆车上。

sentences.en: And I don't know of any more prominent place to carry a message
sentences.zh: 我不知道还有什么比这更显眼的地方可以传达信息了，

sentences.en: than right on the license plate.
sentences.zh: 直接印在车牌上。

sentences.en: That's the best billboard of all.
sentences.zh: 那是最好的广告牌。

sentences.en: In 1971, the slogan on the state's license plate changed from scenic New Hampshire to live free or die.
sentences.zh: 1971年，该州车牌上的标语从“风景优美的新罕布什尔”改成了“不自由，毋宁死”。

sentences.en: But not everyone embraced the state's message.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有人都接受该州的这一口号。

sentences.en: That's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: At 88 years old, George Maynard still gets heated about the New Hampshire license plate.
sentences.zh: 88岁的乔治·梅纳德至今提起新罕布什尔州的车牌仍会感到愤慨。

sentences.en: George grew up in Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 乔治在罗德岛长大。

sentences.en: He married a woman, Maxine, who he'd actually met in junior high.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一位名叫玛克辛的妻子，他们其实在初中时就认识了。

sentences.en: They settled into a pretty typical family life.
sentences.zh: 他们过着相当典型的家庭生活。

sentences.en: They had kids.
sentences.zh: 他们有了孩子。

sentences.en: George got a job as a newspaper printer.
sentences.zh: 乔治找了一份报纸印刷工的工作。

sentences.en: And then something happened, like really abruptly.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件事，非常突然。

sentences.en: George and his family joined the Jehovah's Witnesses.
sentences.zh: 乔治和他的家人加入了耶和华见证人教派。

sentences.en: And by 1972, they had moved to Claremont, New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 到了1972年，他们搬到了新罕布什尔州的克莱蒙特。

sentences.en: That's where the trouble started.
sentences.zh: 麻烦就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: Every day, George would hop in his car and drive to work at the local printing press,
sentences.zh: 每天，乔治都会跳上车去当地的印刷厂上班，

sentences.en: with his New Hampshire license plates screaming, in all caps,
sentences.zh: 车上挂着新罕布什尔州的车牌，上面用全大写字母尖叫着：

sentences.en: LIVE FREE OR DIE.
sentences.zh: “不自由，毋宁死”。

sentences.en: And this really grated on George,
sentences.zh: 这让乔治感到非常刺眼，

sentences.en: because he didn't share Meldrum Thompson's belief of freedom over everything.
sentences.zh: 因为他并不认同梅尔德拉姆·汤普森那种“自由高于一切”的信念。

sentences.en: As a Jehovah's Witness, George actually believed that God-given life
sentences.zh: 作为一名耶和华见证人，乔治实际上认为上帝赋予的生命

sentences.en: was more important than freedom.
sentences.zh: 比自由更重要。

sentences.en: Oh, that's right.
sentences.zh: 噢，没错。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And the real existence of life is very precious.
sentences.zh: 生命的真实存在是非常宝贵的。

sentences.en: Life is a gift.
sentences.zh: 生命是一份礼物。

sentences.en: And we appreciate it very much.
sentences.zh: 我们非常珍惜它。

sentences.en: George didn't want the government telling him what to die for.
sentences.zh: 乔治不想让政府告诉他该为什么而死。

sentences.en: So then one day I decided, you know, if it's offensive,
sentences.zh: 所以有一天我决定，你知道，如果它让人反感，

sentences.en: why should be forced to support something that's offensive?
sentences.zh: 为什么我非要被迫支持某种让人反感的东西呢？

sentences.en: So I covered it up with red tape.
sentences.zh: 于是我用红胶带把它盖住了。

sentences.en: And when he erased the state motto,
sentences.zh: 当他抹去州格言时，

sentences.en: George marched to the front lines of the license plate wars.
sentences.zh: 乔治就走到了车牌战争的最前线。

sentences.en: Covering up the slogan was a violation of state law.
sentences.zh: 遮盖标语违反了州法律。

sentences.en: But a few weeks went by and not much happened.
sentences.zh: 但几周过去了，什么事也没发生。

sentences.en: Until one day, George and Maxine were shopping.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，乔治和玛克辛正在购物。

sentences.en: They left the store, they got to their car in the parking lot,
sentences.zh: 他们离开商店，来到停车场的车旁，

sentences.en: and they saw a police officer writing them a ticket.
sentences.zh: 看到一名警察正在给他们开罚单。

sentences.en: George told me he'd been expecting this for a while.
sentences.zh: 乔治告诉我，他早就预料到会有这一天。

sentences.en: He didn't actually feel scared or surprised.
sentences.zh: 他其实并不感到害怕或惊讶。

sentences.en: Well, I was happy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时很高兴。

sentences.en: You were happy?
sentences.zh: 你很高兴？

sentences.en: Yeah, because I was expressing my belief, my rejection of something.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我在表达我的信仰，表达我对某种事物的拒绝。

sentences.en: George refused to pay the $25 ticket.
sentences.zh: 乔治拒绝缴纳那张25美元的罚单。

sentences.en: And of course...
sentences.zh: 当然……

sentences.en: I kept the tape on.
sentences.zh: 我还是贴着胶带。

sentences.en: I did it again.
sentences.zh: 我又做了一次。

sentences.en: The tickets piled up until his consistent refusal to pay landed him in court.
sentences.zh: 罚单越积越多，直到他始终拒绝缴纳罚款，最终被送上了法庭。

sentences.en: And the judge put him away for 15 days.
sentences.zh: 法官判了他15天监禁。

sentences.en: And so if you don't want to live free or die, you go to jail in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你不想“不自由，毋宁死”，在新罕布什尔州你就会进监狱。

sentences.en: Two weeks may not seem like hard time,
sentences.zh: 两周时间看起来不算长，

sentences.en: but the sentence had a huge impact on George's life.
sentences.zh: 但这次判决对乔治的生活产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: When he didn't show up for work, he got fired.
sentences.zh: 因为没去上班，他被解雇了。

sentences.en: And he was embarrassed that his kids had to see him hauled away.
sentences.zh: 而且他感到很尴尬，因为他的孩子们不得不看着他被带走。

sentences.en: Things were tough for the Maynards.
sentences.zh: 梅纳德一家过得很艰难。

sentences.en: But George still wasn't done fighting.
sentences.zh: 但乔治并没有停止抗争。

sentences.en: With the help of the American Civil Liberties Union,
sentences.zh: 在美国公民自由联盟的帮助下，

sentences.en: he filed suit in New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 他在新罕布什尔州提起诉讼，

sentences.en: claiming the state's law prohibiting the altering of license plates was unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 声称该州禁止涂改车牌的法律违宪。

sentences.en: And the state court agreed.
sentences.zh: 州法院同意了他的观点。

sentences.en: But Meldrum, live free or die, Thompson, had become governor by then.
sentences.zh: 但此时，“不自由，毋宁死”的梅尔德拉姆·汤普森已经当上了州长。

sentences.en: And Thompson was not inclined to extend George the freedom to cover up his beloved motto.
sentences.zh: 汤普森并不打算给予乔治遮盖他心爱格言的自由。

sentences.en: So Thompson appealed the case.
sentences.zh: 于是汤普森对该案提起了上诉。

sentences.en: All the way to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 一直上诉到美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院。

sentences.en: 75-14-53, Willie against Maynard.
sentences.zh: 75-14-53，威利诉梅纳德案。

sentences.en: The license plates collided with the First Amendment before the High Court in November of 1976.
sentences.zh: 1976年11月，车牌问题在最高法院与第一修正案发生了碰撞。

sentences.en: During oral arguments, George Maynard's lawyer claimed that in covering up Live Free or Die,
sentences.zh: 在口头辩论中，乔治·梅纳德的律师声称，遮盖“不自由，毋宁死”的行为，

sentences.en: George was just exercising his freedom of expression.
sentences.zh: 乔治只是在行使他的言论自由。

sentences.en: License plates are displayed on people's private vehicles.
sentences.zh: 车牌是展示在人们的私家车上的。

sentences.en: He argued the government can't just hijack that space and force people to express a certain viewpoint.
sentences.zh: 他辩称，政府不能随意劫持那个空间，强迫人们表达某种观点。

sentences.en: And it's our position that the state lacks the power to require its citizens to bear this sort of motto.
sentences.zh: 我们的立场是，州政府没有权力要求其公民背负这种格言。

sentences.en: I think that if the court were to uphold this sort of thing,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果法院支持这种做法，

sentences.en: then the state could require all citizens to wear a pin or an armband.
sentences.zh: 那么州政府就可以要求所有公民佩戴徽章或臂章。

sentences.en: Or they could require you to have a plaque on your door next to your address saying live free or die.
sentences.zh: 或者他们可以要求你在门上的地址旁边挂一块牌子，上面写着“不自由，毋宁死”。

sentences.en: New Hampshire countered with,
sentences.zh: 新罕布什尔州反驳道：

sentences.en: what's the big deal?
sentences.zh: 这有什么大不了的？

sentences.en: Just because it's on the license plate doesn't mean every driver believes in it.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为它印在车牌上，并不意味着每个司机都相信它。

sentences.en: And sometimes it seemed like the court was buying it.
sentences.zh: 有时看起来法院似乎也接受了这种说法。

sentences.en: Like Justice Thurgood Marshall.
sentences.zh: 比如瑟古德·马歇尔大法官。

sentences.en: The first time I noticed Martell was after this case was filed.
sentences.zh: 我第一次注意到马歇尔是在这个案子提起之后。

sentences.en: I had never paid any attention to it.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未关注过它。

sentences.en: I noticed New Hampshire license.
sentences.zh: 我注意到了新罕布什尔州的车牌。

sentences.en: I said, well, it's about New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，那是关于新罕布什尔州的。

sentences.en: But I didn't live or die about it.
sentences.zh: 但我并不觉得非要“不自由，毋宁死”。

sentences.en: Well, most people in New Hampshire don't either.
sentences.zh: 嗯，新罕布什尔州的大多数人也不觉得。

sentences.en: They accept it.
sentences.zh: 他们接受了它。

sentences.en: So what was it?
sentences.zh: 那它到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: Was the license plate a declaration of the state's ideology?
sentences.zh: 车牌是该州意识形态的宣言吗？

sentences.en: Or just a thing that says nothing at all?
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅是一个什么都没表达的东西？

sentences.en: Since everybody had one.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都有一个。

sentences.en: George couldn't make it to D.C.
sentences.zh: 乔治没能去华盛顿特区

sentences.en: for the ruling.
sentences.zh: 参加裁决。

sentences.en: He actually found out the same way as everyone else.
sentences.zh: 他其实和其他人一样，是通过同样的方式得知的。

sentences.en: From CBS News headquarters in New York,
sentences.zh: 来自纽约的哥伦比亚广播公司新闻总部，

sentences.en: this is the CBS Evening News with Walter Cronkite.
sentences.zh: 这是沃尔特·克朗凯特主持的CBS晚间新闻。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court ruled today that drivers may not be compelled to...
sentences.zh: 最高法院今天裁定，司机不得被强迫……

sentences.en: Cronkite came on the news and says that
sentences.zh: 克朗凯特在新闻中说，

sentences.en: the Supreme Court ruled in our favor that you can tape over the state models.
sentences.zh: 最高法院做出了有利于我们的裁决，你可以用胶带盖住州格言。

sentences.en: And so, that was nice.
sentences.zh: 所以，那很好。

sentences.en: The court, in effect, gave them permission to tape over the offensive words.
sentences.zh: 法院实际上准许了他们用胶带盖住那些令人反感的文字。

sentences.en: I think the court got it right in the Maynard case.
sentences.zh: 我认为法院在梅纳德案中的判决是正确的。

sentences.en: Caroline Mala Corbin is a First Amendment scholar at the University of Miami.
sentences.zh: 卡罗琳·马拉·科尔宾是迈阿密大学的第一修正案学者。

sentences.en: She says the court's 6-3 decision hinged on a concept called compelled speech.
sentences.zh: 她说，法院6比3的裁决取决于一个叫做“被迫言论”的概念。

sentences.en: The First Amendment protects both your right to speak.
sentences.zh: 第一修正案保护你的言论权利。

sentences.en: So it protects you against government censorship.
sentences.zh: 所以它保护你免受政府审查。

sentences.en: But the free speech clause also protects your right not to speak.
sentences.zh: 但言论自由条款也保护你“不说话”的权利。

sentences.en: So it protects you against the government,
sentences.zh: 所以它保护你免受政府的侵害，

sentences.en: forcing you to say an ideological message that you disagree with.
sentences.zh: 强迫你说出你不同意的意识形态信息。

sentences.en: And that was what the problem was here.
sentences.zh: 而这正是这里的问题所在。

sentences.en: They were trying to force you to say something that you don't want to say,
sentences.zh: 他们试图强迫你说出你不想说的话，

sentences.en: and you don't want to live by.
sentences.zh: 而且你不想按照它去生活。

sentences.en: In George's homemade solution, that strip of red tape,
sentences.zh: 在乔治自制的解决方案中，那一小条红胶带，

sentences.en: it actually held up under the weight of the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 它实际上经受住了第一修正案的考验。

sentences.en: And so, that's my way of expressing my free speech.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我表达言论自由的方式。

sentences.en: At this point, it might seem like George Maynard's case solved the license plate problem.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，乔治·梅纳德的案子似乎解决了车牌问题。

sentences.en: Today, if you live in, say, New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 今天，如果你住在，比如说，新泽西州，

sentences.en: and object to the notion that you live in the Garden State,
sentences.zh: 并且反对你住在“花园之州”的说法，

sentences.en: well, you can cover that sucker up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以把那个鬼东西盖住。

sentences.en: Your car is not a government billboard on wheels.
sentences.zh: 你的车不是轮子上的政府广告牌。

sentences.en: But it turns out the constitutional battle over license plates is not over.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，关于车牌的宪法之争并没有结束。

sentences.en: Because after all that was settled, a new problem showed up.
sentences.zh: 因为在这一切解决之后，又出现了一个新问题。

sentences.en: Specialty plates.
sentences.zh: 特色车牌。

sentences.en: You've seen these.
sentences.zh: 你见过这些。

sentences.en: Unlike vanity plates, where drivers choose their own numbers and letters,
sentences.zh: 与司机自选数字和字母的个性化车牌不同，

sentences.en: specialty plates sport alternate designs with their own logos and slogans.
sentences.zh: 特色车牌采用带有各自标志和口号的替代设计。

sentences.en: They're usually put out in collaboration with the government
sentences.zh: 它们通常是由非政府组织与政府合作推出的。

sentences.en: by a non-governmental organization.
sentences.zh: 当司机选择特色车牌时，他们会多付一点钱。

sentences.en: When drivers choose a specialty plate, they pay a little extra.
sentences.zh: 这些收益会在他们选择的组织和州机动车管理局之间进行分配。

sentences.en: And those proceeds get split between their chosen group
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，在我们家，我们有一块“拯救海牛”的车牌。

sentences.en: and the State Department of Motor Vehicles.
sentences.zh: 那是佛罗里达州提供的一种特色车牌，

sentences.en: So, for example, in my family, we have a Save the Manatees license plate.
sentences.zh: 我们多付了钱才买到的。

sentences.en: That's a specialty license plate that the state of Florida offers
sentences.zh: 你为什么选择海牛车牌？

sentences.en: that we paid extra money to purchase.
sentences.zh: 这是什么荒谬的问题。

sentences.en: Why did you choose the manatee plate?
sentences.zh: 我们当然想拯救海牛。

sentences.en: What are ridiculous questions.
sentences.zh: 特色车牌是轻松赚钱的工具。

sentences.en: We want to save a manatee, naturally.
sentences.zh: 我们当然想拯救海牛。

sentences.en: Specialty plates are easy money.
sentences.zh: 特色车牌是轻松赚钱的工具。

sentences.en: A lot of states will issue one to almost any non-profit,
sentences.zh: 许多州几乎会向任何非营利组织发放特色车牌，

sentences.en: as long as enough people are interested.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够多的人感兴趣就行。

sentences.en: But the problem with an open-door policy is you might not like who comes inside.
sentences.zh: 但“敞开大门”政策的问题在于，你可能并不喜欢进来的人。

sentences.en: And a decade ago, the state of Texas learned that the hard way.
sentences.zh: 十年前，德克萨斯州就深刻地体会到了这一点。

sentences.en: I'm now calling the meeting for November 10, 2011,
sentences.zh: 我现在宣布召开2011年11月10日的会议，

sentences.en: of the board of the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles to order.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州机动车管理局董事会会议现在开始。

sentences.en: Usually, public hearings for the DMV are dull, bureaucratic affairs, poorly attended.
sentences.zh: 通常，机动车管理局的公开听证会都是枯燥乏味的官僚事务，出席人数寥寥。

sentences.en: But in 2011, the board of the Texas DMV held a standing-room-only hearing.
sentences.zh: 但在2011年，德克萨斯州机动车管理局董事会举行了一场座无虚席的听证会。

sentences.en: So, we're going to move to Agenda Item 5A, which is the approval of a specialty license plate.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们现在进入议程第5A项，即关于批准一款特色车牌的议题。

sentences.en: The DMV board votes on proposed designs for specialty plates.
sentences.zh: 机动车管理局董事会对提议的特色车牌设计进行投票。

sentences.en: They generally approve the designs with very little fanfare or scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会毫无波澜或审查地批准这些设计。

sentences.en: But this one was different.
sentences.zh: 但这次不同。

sentences.en: The Sons of Confederate Veterans wanted Texas to issue a license plate featuring the Confederate battle flag.
sentences.zh: “邦联退伍军人之子”组织希望德克萨斯州发放一款印有邦联战旗的车牌。

sentences.en: And a lot of people weren't happy about it.
sentences.zh: 很多人对此感到不满。

sentences.en: Dozens of community leaders showed up to testify.
sentences.zh: 数十位社区领袖到场作证。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for letting me come.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢让我发言。

sentences.en: That voice you're hearing is Sanfronia Thompson.
sentences.zh: 你刚才听到的声音是桑弗罗尼亚·汤普森。

sentences.en: She's a Texas Statehouse representative and a black woman born in 1939.
sentences.zh: 她是德克萨斯州众议院议员，也是一位出生于1939年的黑人女性。

sentences.en: There was a time that I could not even come on the grounds of the Capitol because I was black.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我甚至因为是黑人而无法踏入州议会大厦的土地。

sentences.en: And it's very difficult to be able to see these symbols because they bring back memories.
sentences.zh: 看到这些符号非常痛苦，因为它们勾起了往事。

sentences.en: And to me, it's like sticking poop in the face of black people every day to see them.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，每天看到它们就像是把屎糊在黑人的脸上一样。

sentences.en: And that's how repulsive it is.
sentences.zh: 这就是它有多令人反感。

sentences.en: We have folks who say, well, I'm offended by the SCV plate.
sentences.zh: 我们有些人会说，好吧，我被“邦联退伍军人之子”的车牌冒犯了。

sentences.en: And my response is, and your point?
sentences.zh: 而我的回应是，那又怎样？

sentences.en: In favor of the Confederate flag plates was Jerry Patterson.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·帕特森支持邦联旗车牌。

sentences.en: He's the commissioner of the Texas Land Office and a member of the Sons of Confederate Veterans.

sentences.en: And once again, there was a lot at stake here.

sentences.en: So, as early as 1916, Massachusetts was stamping their plates out of tin, which was way cheaper.

sentences.en: So, these mass-produced metal plates, they hit the scene, and that's when, you know, license plates, as we talk about in the story, basically become billboards.
sentences.zh: 于是，这些大规模生产的金属车牌出现了，正如我们在故事里提到的，车牌基本上变成了广告牌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They become this space where states can play around with graphics and slogans, and Stuart has thousands of examples.
sentences.zh: 它们成了各州可以发挥图形和标语创意的空间，斯图尔特就有成千上万个样本。

sentences.en: So, during our interview, he was, you know, pulling out plate after plate after plate.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们的采访中，他不停地拿出一块又一块车牌。

sentences.en: Like, I would try to ask him a question, and he would, you know, throw off a one-word answer, but already be pulling out the next graphic plate to show me.
sentences.zh: 比如，我试着问他一个问题，他会随口给出一个字的回答，但手里已经拿出了下一块有图案的车牌给我看。

sentences.en: This is a golden jubilee from the state of Washington from 1939.
sentences.zh: 这是1939年华盛顿州的金禧纪念车牌。

sentences.en: The 36th Wyoming was the first year of the Bucking Bronco.
sentences.zh: 怀俄明州1936年的车牌是第一年使用“野马”图案。

sentences.en: Mount Rushmore in 1952 was on the plate.
sentences.zh: 1952年的车牌上印有拉什莫尔山。

sentences.en: It was the first year of the state-shaped plate in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 那是田纳西州第一年使用州轮廓形状的车牌。

sentences.en: South Carolina in 1930, they're the iodine state.
sentences.zh: 1930年的南卡罗来纳州，他们是“碘之州”。

sentences.en: Where they, like, produce iodine?
sentences.zh: 他们是生产碘吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Here's the New York World's Fair.
sentences.zh: 这是纽约世博会的车牌。

sentences.en: No real graphics, but it does have a lot of words on it.
sentences.zh: 没有真正的图形，但上面确实有很多字。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's kind of fun to hear all the experimentation that was going on.
sentences.zh: 听到当时所有的这些试验过程真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Like, the Tennessee plate was shaped like Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 比如，田纳西州的车牌形状就是田纳西州的轮廓。

sentences.en: That's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那真的很酷。

sentences.en: Yeah, he said that one was actually pretty tough to mount on people's cars.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他说那块车牌其实很难安装在车上。

sentences.en: I bet.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定。

sentences.en: Yeah, but, you know, that experimentation really exploded in the 1970s when states started putting a reflective coating on the license plates.
sentences.zh: 是的，但你知道，这种试验在20世纪70年代真正爆发了，当时各州开始在车牌上涂反光涂层。

sentences.en: And that basically let them print really detailed graphics rather than having to, like, emboss the shapes into the metal.
sentences.zh: 这基本上让他们可以印制非常详细的图形，而不必像以前那样把形状压印在金属上。

sentences.en: So, designs got really busy.
sentences.zh: 所以，设计变得非常繁杂。

sentences.en: And I think that is perhaps best exemplified by the plates that Illinois recently introduced just back in 2017.
sentences.zh: 我认为伊利诺伊州在2017年刚推出的车牌就是最好的例子。

sentences.en: So, let's pull that one up.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们把那块拿出来看看。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, there's a lot going on here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面的内容非常多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It has the light blue and red of the Chicago flag, which I like.
sentences.zh: 它有芝加哥旗帜的浅蓝色和红色，我很喜欢。

sentences.en: That looks like the top of the statehouse, I'm assuming.
sentences.zh: 我想那看起来像是州议会大厦的顶部。

sentences.en: And I know a windmill.
sentences.zh: 我还看到了一个风车。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Shout out to rural Illinois.
sentences.zh: 向伊利诺伊州的农村地区致敬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because right next to that is the Chicago skyline.
sentences.zh: 因为就在那旁边是芝加哥的天际线。

sentences.en: And then, of course, at the very far left edge is half a face of Abraham Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，在最左边的边缘是亚伯拉罕·林肯的半张脸。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, there's not even enough room for him.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至连放他的空间都不够了。

sentences.en: He's, like, split right down the nose.
sentences.zh: 他就像是从鼻子中间被劈开了一样。

sentences.en: And it has Land of Lincoln, of course, which is their motto.
sentences.zh: 而且上面当然还有他们的座右铭“林肯之地”。

sentences.en: What's kind of interesting about this is, like, this is kind of the opposite of the Idaho potato problem that we talked about in the piece.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这有点像我们在节目中讨论的爱达荷州土豆问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not the whole state boiled down into one thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是把整个州浓缩成一件事物。

sentences.en: This is the whole state boiled down into way too many things to put on a license plate.
sentences.zh: 这是把整个州浓缩成了太多东西，以至于根本塞不进一块车牌里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not pretty because it's not like the canvas gets any bigger.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不好看，因为画布并没有变大。

sentences.en: It's still just this half a square foot and you're cramming ever more onto it.
sentences.zh: 它仍然只有半平方英尺大，而你却在往上面塞越来越多的东西。

sentences.en: And so, what do, you know, people like Stuart, you know, license plate collectors make of, you know, this kind of graphical onslaught?
sentences.zh: 那么，像斯图尔特这样的车牌收藏家对这种图形轰炸有什么看法呢？

sentences.en: Like, what do they think of this as compared to the old plates?
sentences.zh: 比起旧车牌，他们怎么看这个？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, most collectors I talked to expressed a preference for those older plates with the simple, sleek design.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我采访的大多数收藏家都表示更喜欢那些设计简洁、流畅的旧车牌。

sentences.en: But a lot of them also just take the whole thing in stride because to guys like Stuart, the more the merrier, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们中的许多人也只是泰然处之，因为对于像斯图尔特这样的人来说，越多越好，对吧？

sentences.en: Do you think license plate design has gotten, like, too busy and complicated?
sentences.zh: 你认为车牌设计变得太繁杂、太复杂了吗？

sentences.en: Um, no, I don't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Here's the neat plate.
sentences.zh: 这儿有一块很棒的车牌。

sentences.en: This is one of my favorites.
sentences.zh: 这是我的最爱之一。

sentences.en: It's the Georgia peach.
sentences.zh: 是佐治亚州的桃子车牌。

sentences.en: Um, what else do I have that I can show you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我还有什么可以给你看的呢？

sentences.en: More graphics just means more plates.
sentences.zh: 更多的图形只意味着更多的车牌。

sentences.en: It just means more joy for Stuart.
sentences.zh: 这只意味着斯图尔特能得到更多的快乐。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Just more grist for the collector's mail.
sentences.zh: 这只是收藏家邮寄清单上的更多素材而已。

sentences.en: Here's a Texas Centennial plate from 1936.
sentences.zh: 这是1936年的德克萨斯州百年纪念车牌。

sentences.en: Here's New Mexico, 1940.
sentences.zh: 这是1940年的新墨西哥州车牌。

sentences.en: Great graphics on these.
sentences.zh: 这些上面的图形很棒。

sentences.en: Utah, center scenic America in 1942.
sentences.zh: 1942年犹他州的“美国风景中心”车牌。

sentences.en: Ohio in 1938.
sentences.zh: 1938年的俄亥俄州车牌。

sentences.en: Early graphic plate from Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 罗德岛州早期的图形车牌。

sentences.en: 41 Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 41年的夏威夷车牌。

sentences.en: Here's an Oklahoma plate with an F in the middle.
sentences.zh: 这是一块中间带字母F的俄克拉荷马州车牌。
